tradeInReducesBase.note: Dealers charge sales tax on the net price after the trade-in allowance. A trade-in reduces the base when the traded vehicle goes into the dealer's inventory in a single transaction. A rebate is taxable when it is not shown on the original bill of sale.

content.intro: {state} charges {stateRate} state sales tax plus a local city, county or district tax. Registration is paid every year by weight, and counties bill a yearly property tax on the vehicle.

howItWorks.text: The state rate is {stateRate}. Sales tax is figured on the net price after your trade-in allowance when you buy from a dealer.
The local rate depends on where the dealer is located for a dealer sale, and on your registration address for a private or out-of-state purchase.
If you paid sales tax in another state, you get credit for it against the Kansas tax, up to the Kansas amount, with proof of the tax paid.

faq.q: Does a trade-in lower the sales tax in Kansas?
faq.text: Yes, for a dealer sale the tax is figured on the net price after the trade-in allowance. A rebate that is not on the original bill of sale is taxable.
For a dealer sale it is the combined rate where the dealer is located. For a private or out-of-state purchase it is the rate for your registration address.

faq.q: Is the yearly property tax included?
faq.text: No. Each county applies its own mill levy to the vehicle's value, so the amount depends on your county and the vehicle.
